title: Kumrat Waterfall
subtitle: Roadside fall in the Kumrat valley, Upper Dir

landmark.name: Kumrat Waterfall
edits: The fall is drawn on the real slope: no terrace is cut (terrace 0). The stream line runs from a lip at DEM 2520 m down to a plunge pool at the foot, about 210 m long and about 120 m of drop measured from the Copernicus DEM (30 m DSM, approximate; the DSM smooths the chute and cannot show a lip, so the drop is an estimate and may be too large or small).

The falling water (four translucent sheets with scrolling streaks), the mist at the foot, the plunge pool (a flat disc about 16 m across) and the dark wet boulders beside the chute are illustrative paint.
The stream itself is not mapped in OSM (no waterway within the box except the Panjkora River, about 200 m west); its line is the DEM steepest-descent line through the gully.
The OSM waterfall node (waterway=waterfall, id 6534025186) is at 35.569517, 72.192008, 0.1 m from the place point and is used as the landmark point.
The drive is the Kumrat valley road (OSM tertiary, ref S-16); the trailhead is its nearest mapped vertex to the fall, about 180 m away. The walk to the foot (about 110 m) is traced over the DEM.
